processing: Fully oxidised black tea, most often sold as a small BOP grade, including CTC.
harvest_season: No garden-specific calendar is documented; as with other Assam gardens, the May to June second flush is generally the most valued.
appearance_dry: Small, dark broken leaf or granules, typical of BOP and CTC.
taste_profile: Strong and full-bodied with marked maltiness and a rich colour.

brewing.notes: Small leaf gives up everything in a single steep. Two to three minutes is enough, with milk if you like.

vintage_note: Mostly reaches shoppers as a BOP from wholesale and blending-oriented sellers, often with no year on the label. As usual for broken Assam grades, buy fresh stock and use it within about a year.
description:
Keyhung is an estate in Tinsukia district of Upper Assam, south of the Brahmaputra. It reaches shoppers mainly as a plain BOP tea, sold for its strength and not for any fine-leaf character.

Small leaf and full oxidation give the cup its colour and strength quickly. One seller states that 60 percent of the estate is clonal.

The tea is strong, malty and dark, and suits a morning mug with milk. Keep it to a single short steep, because a long one tips it into harshness.

There are few specifics on the label, so buy from a seller who turns stock over quickly. Ignore health claims attached to it, and treat seller figures about the estate as rough.
history: Little is documented about the garden, and its present ownership could not be confirmed. Seller descriptions are the main record of it.
